statusText: Tail eases to 22%. Mapped policy state: WATCH. The 31,119.75 session low printed in the prior hour is unextended, NQ Dec26 has recovered to 31,181.00 and the loss has narrowed to -0.70% from -0.78%, while VIX slipped to 15.71 from a 16.02 session high. Record Strait of Hormuz tanker strikes still hold Brent near 105 and WTI near 92.6 at roughly +4.9%, and the 10-year sits at 5.33% with the 30-year at 5.70% near a 24-year peak, so Stress rises to 66% in the high band.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH with Tail at 22%, inside the 20-24% band and below the 25% blocking threshold. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 13:30Z-16:00Z, spanning the U.S. cash open and the first two cash hours, where conditional Tail peaks at 26% and maps to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Conditional Tail eases to 23% by the 16:00Z window close, lifts to 24% across the 17:00Z 30-year auction and the 17:40Z Fed Musalem speech, and returns to the EA_ON band from 20:00Z as the cash session completes. Stress at 66% is the dominant reading: the environment is difficult and may still mean-revert. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold above an unextended session low as the Hormuz oil shock and a 24-year-high 30-year yield keep Stress high while Tail eases
body:
The thirteenth Globex hour of the Oct 7-8 session did not confirm the prior hour's breakdown. NQ Dec26 trades 31,181.00 as of 12:18Z, -221.25 or -0.70% against a 31,402.25 prior close, corroborated independently at 31,180.50 with a matching -0.71% and the same 31,402.25 reference. The 31,119.75 low that printed in the 11:00Z hour has stood for more than an hour, price sits roughly 61 points above it, and the day's loss has narrowed from -0.78%. VIX has eased to 15.71, +4.18%, from a 16.02 session high. Yesterday's cash session told the same story: the Nasdaq-100 traded down to 30,904.46 and closed at 31,160.08, near the top of its range.

That combination is why Tail steps down to 22% rather than through the 25% blocking threshold. A session low that goes unextended for an hour while the loss narrows and implied volatility backs off its high is a failed downside extension, which is the opposite of the repeated extension after failed retracements that defines a pathological price path. A sub-16 VIX is not the volatility signature of a sustained no-retracement trend, and the 1.10% overnight range is an orderly repricing.

The amplifier stack behind Stress is nonetheless fully intact and broadened this hour. A record week of Strait of Hormuz tanker strikes, with at least one attack a day reported since October 2 and tanker transits at their lowest since July, holds Brent near 105 and WTI near 92.6, both around +4.9%. A tropical system is expected to reach the U.S. Gulf refining coast by Friday, and Chevron is evacuating nonessential offshore personnel, adding a second supply channel to the geopolitical one. Energy-driven inflation expectations have carried the 2-year to 4.82%, the 10-year to 5.33% and the 30-year to 5.70%, just under a 24-year 5.73% peak. Taiwan Semiconductor is down 2.09% premarket. Against that, the IEA has agreed to accelerate oil stock releases, which gives the energy impulse a visible counterweight.

Under the inherited contract this is an aligned amplifier stack that has not yet produced observed one-way structure, so it raises Stress to 66% in the high band and leaves Tail in the watch band. The forward risk is concentrated rather than diffuse. The 13:30Z cash open and the first two cash hours carry conditional Tail to 26% because an opening auction that extends lower on shallow pullbacks would be the session's first genuine directional evidence. The 30-year auction near 17:02Z is the day's clearest unresolved delayed second-leg mechanism: a weak tail pushing the long bond above 5.73% could transmit into equities with a lag, which is exactly the structurally multi-stage sequence that warrants care. Both are conditional branches, not observed facts.

Evidence quality supports Confidence at 88%. The futures level, prior close and session range are independently corroborated across two providers, VIX and the cash index close are verified, the full 2Y/10Y/30Y curve is verified, oil is verified from two sources, and the seven-day U.S. calendar is verified. Two gaps are explicit: the shared Finviz context file is nine days stale and partial, so it was disregarded entirely, and the 12:30Z initial jobless claims actual could not be verified at the assessment cutoff, so it remains a scheduled calendar item with an unknown outcome rather than published news.

lookbackSummary: The 24 hours to 12:00Z trace one full risk cycle. Tail ran 21-23% through Wednesday's European and early U.S. hours, eased steadily to a 10% trough by 03:00Z as the overnight session mean-reverted, then rebuilt from 06:00Z as the Hormuz oil shock and the long-end yield move reasserted themselves, reaching 23% at 11:00Z when a three-hour base at 31,196.75 gave way to a 31,119.75 low. Stress rose almost monotonically across the window, from 51% to 65%, which is the clearer signal: the environment deteriorated steadily while the price path kept retracing. Every hour stayed in the EA_ON or WATCH band and no hour reached the 25% blocking threshold.
outlookSummary: Conditional Tail is concentrated in the U.S. cash session rather than spread across the window. It rises from 22% now to a 26% peak in the 14:00Z first full cash hour, holds 25% at 15:00Z, and those two hours are the only slots mapping to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES; the 13:30Z-16:00Z danger window covers them. A secondary 24% ridge at 17:00Z spans the 30-year auction and the Fed Musalem speech, reflecting a credible delayed second-leg mechanism rather than observed structure. From 20:00Z the cash close returns Tail to the EA_ON band, and it bottoms at 13% through Asian hours before drifting back to 18% by Friday mid-morning as European and U.S. positioning resumes. Stress stays in the high band through the cash session, easing to the elevated band overnight but never returning to the low-50s of early Thursday, because neither the Hormuz supply risk nor the long-end yield level is resolved inside this window. Confidence decays from 88% to 75% with distance from the observed evidence.
